checkpoints.description: Task 'iris-cycle-03' completed successfully.

[1/4] Progression and saves: count title and chamber progress only for real campaign chambers, so a forged or stale save with ghost ids cannot inflate lit chambers or stars, proven by a forged-save screenshot pair and a reload run

impact_assessment.why: normalizeProgress keeps any non-empty level id, and solvedCount/starCount count every stored key. A save containing ghost ids shows lit chambers and stars for chambers that do not exist, while the chamber grid shows none, so the title and index disagree.
impact_assessment.benefits: The title, rank and chamber index summarize only the 12 authored chambers; older or hand-edited saves keep their real entries and ignore invented ones; the fix is a two-function signature change with no storage-format change.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: progress keys stay under iris.progress.v1; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: read-only filtering, no record rewrite.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add failing progress tests for a ghost entry and a missing campaign list, pass LEVELS from the two app call sites, and verify the title and chambers screen from the same forged localStorage record before and after.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Levels: give The Vault two wall blocks that frame the chamber, teach the wall tile in the field guide and README, and prove the episode finale still solves at par 4 with a before/after board pair and a played run

impact_assessment.why: The engine validates, renders and tests walls, but no chamber uses one, so the wall tile is dead content and The Vault reads as an empty 7x7 frame with four floating mirrors. The chamber named The Vault has no vault structure.
impact_assessment.benefits: The Episode I finale gains visual structure and finally exercises the wall renderer; the field guide and symbol table explain that walls stop a beam; the existing unique four-move solution and par stay unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: level rows and solver par are frozen by tests; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save-format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Place walls only on cells that no solution beam crosses, verify the stored solution and the true minimum with check-levels and the solver suite, add a UI assertion for the wall copy, and replay the chamber end to end.

checkpoints.description: Task 'iris-cycle-05' completed successfully.

[1/4] Input feel: add Z/R/H keyboard shortcuts for undo, reset and hint, document them in the field guide and README, and prove them with a keyboard-only browser run plus a before/after help dialog pair

impact_assessment.why: The board supports arrow keys and Enter/Space, but undo, reset and hint still require a pointer. A keyboard-only player can rotate but cannot recover, restart or ask for a hint without leaving the keys.
impact_assessment.benefits: The three recovery actions get single-key shortcuts that stay out of the way of typing, dialogs and modified chords; the field guide and aria-keyshortcuts make the bindings discoverable and screen-reader visible.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no runtime dependency or save change; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: shortcuts must not fire behind an open dialog or after a win.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Guard the handler on the game screen, an open dialog, a winning board and modifier keys; add a browser run that presses Z, H and R; keep Enter/Space and pointer behavior unchanged.

[2/4]-[3/4] Added episode-final helpers, the win-episode callout and finale copy, with a failing-first helper test, two preview checks, and a real The Vault to Yellow Room played run

[1/4] Progression pass 2: mark each episode finale and the campaign finale in the victory dialog, proven by same-state The Vault and White Crown pairs plus a played The Vault to Yellow Room transition

impact_assessment.why: The fourth chamber of each episode and the twelfth chamber end a chapter, but their victory dialogs use the same ordinary Chamber NN complete copy as every other chamber, so the player gets no signal that a new episode or the end of the campaign has arrived.
impact_assessment.benefits: Episode I, II and III finales name the closing episode and the next one, and the twelfth chamber names the campaign complete; the copy is derived from the authored level order so future edits cannot desync it.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: level order and par remain frozen; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save-format change, preview victories still record nothing.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add pure episode-final helpers with tests, use them in finishLevel, check both previews in the browser dogfood, and play The Vault through to the Next transition.
